post.description:
Creates a headless onramp order. Caller passes customer + provider + payment method and receives a method-specific payload in paymentMethodResponseDetails:

- ACH/SEPA/PIX → bank-transfer details to display.
- CREDIT_DEBIT_CARD → a provider-hosted widget, or `NativeSdkOrder` when renderMode=SDK_NATIVE.
- `responseKind` SDK_BOOTSTRAP (a method on a provider native SDK) → one `NativeSdkOrder` shape whose `clientConfiguration` configures that SDK; `paymentMethodType` selects the method. `destinationNetworkCode` and `X-Idempotency-Key` are required. Continue the order with POST /crypto/order/headless/onramp/{serviceProvider}/{orderId}/actions.
- MERCURYO + APPLE_PAY → native (non-widget) flow: a `sessionToken` (JWT) + `merchantTransactionId`. No redirect URL. The caller renders the Apple Pay sheet itself (Safari/WebView via ApplePaySession) and drives these endpoints, authenticated with header `X-Crypto-Session-Token: <sessionToken>`: on `onvalidatemerchant` call POST /crypto/session/mercuryo/apple-pay/validate-merchant with the event's validationURL; on `onpaymentauthorized` call POST /crypto/session/mercuryo/apple-pay/process with the Apple payToken + the `merchantTransactionId` from this response. The Mercuryo buy_token is fetched and stored server-side, so the caller never handles it. If native Apple Pay is unavailable for the route the call fails with INVALID_PAYMENT_METHOD (no redirect fallback).
- `presentation` PROVIDER_HOSTED → a provider-hosted `paymentLinkUrl` that opens the wallet sheet. Providers that declare pre-order evidence (see `GET /crypto/onramp/{serviceProvider}/requirements`) need the customer's verified email and phone, and acceptance of the agreements that endpoint lists. Acceptance receipts recorded with `POST /accounts/terms-of-service/acceptances` under the customer's `externalId` are read first; without receipts for every code, a valid `verification.agreementAcceptedAt` is accepted instead.

Refusals for a provider that declares pre-order evidence. Each has one recovery:

| Code | HTTP | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` | 403 | Nothing reserved. `errors` lists every unmet item (`email`, `phone`, `agreement`: `MISSING` or `STALE`). Verify, then resend the same request. |
| `LEGAL_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` | 403 | Nothing reserved; only the agreement is unmet. Record the acceptance or send a fresh `verification.agreementAcceptedAt`, then resend. |
| `CUSTOMER_NOT_PAYMENT_READY` | 422 | Nothing reserved. `errors` names `limitUpgrade: REQUIRED`, `PENDING` or `BLOCKED`; complete the process `/requirements` declares, then resend the same request. |
| `TRANSACTION_REQUEST_VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | A malformed or future-dated `agreementAcceptedAt`, even when receipts are on file. Fix the request. |
| `CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE` | 500 | Nothing reserved. Retry the same request later. |
| `HEADLESS_PROVIDER_REJECTED` | 422 | The provider refused a reserved order, so it is spent. Re-verify any channel `errors` lists as `REJECTED`, then create a new order with a new `X-Idempotency-Key` and `externalOrderId`. `serviceProviderDetails` carries `serviceProvider` and `errorType`. |

get.description: Returns the provider's customer-verification requirements and legal agreements. Pass customerId to additionally get the customer's current (advisory) per-field verification status. Pass the order you intend to create — payment method, amount and corridor — to additionally get the provider's own outstanding KYC details: those are jurisdiction-, amount- and method-dependent, so they can only be reported against a concrete intent. providerKycTiming indicates whether provider KYC is discovered before create, during order continuation, or both; an empty pre-order list is not a final KYC verdict. For a provider whose create checks contact and agreement evidence before the order, verificationRequirements also declares verifyWith and agreement, and customerStatus reads the same verification handles and acceptance receipts create reads. customerStatus.agreement.satisfied means receipts cover every code agreement.codes lists; a create that carries a valid verification.agreementAcceptedAt is accepted without them. customerStatus.unavailable and policyUnavailable mark a read that failed; policyUnavailable also marks a policy that create cannot use. With customerId, requirements lists the same steps as one ordered checklist, each with its type, status and the call that clears it; with a whole order intent it starts with ORDER_ROUTE, whether create takes the order before looking at KYC. A step whose state Meld could not read is UNKNOWN, with a reason and no action. eligible is false when a PRE_ORDER step is REQUIRED, PENDING or BLOCKED; true only with a whole order intent and every PRE_ORDER step SATISFIED, which means the checks create makes before it reserves the order pass; absent otherwise, so an order may still be tried. Create stays the authoritative gate. This answers provider KYC for onramp, virtual-account onramp and offramp alike: for a virtual account or an offramp, send customerId only. A provider with no check of its own and no pre-order evidence (Noah, Due, Brale) then gets eligible without an order intent; it covers KYC only, not whether the provider offers the product.

post.description:
Creates a headless offramp order. Caller passes customer + provider + source crypto + fiat payout method and receives a provider-issued wallet address to send cryptocurrency to.

**Customer.** Name the customer by `customerId` (Meld's id) or `externalCustomerId` (yours). With `externalCustomerId` alone the order is for your customer with that id, created on first use with nothing but the id, so a mistyped id makes a new customer rather than a 404. Both together must name the same customer (INCOMPATIBLE_REQUEST otherwise); neither is CUSTOMER_ID_REQUIRED.

**Your order reference.** `externalOrderId` (optional) is your reference for the order, unique per account: one an earlier order already carries is EXTERNAL_ORDER_ID_NOT_UNIQUE, checked before any provider call. It is echoed on the order status, the order's transactions and its webhooks.

**Response.** `status` is the order's lifecycle status as stored (`AWAITING_DEPOSIT` for a new order), the same value GET /crypto/order/{orderId}/status returns.

**Refund wallet.** `refundWalletAddress` is where a deposit is returned if the order is refunded. It must be an address on the source currency's chain (SOURCE_WALLET_INVALID otherwise), may differ from `sourceWalletAddress`, and cannot be changed once the order exists. Accounts whose orders are held to a quote must send `quoteId`, `destinationAmount` and `refundWalletAddress` on every order.

**From a quote.** Send `quoteId` (the `id` of a POST /payments/partner/quote response; an id from POST /payments/crypto/quote is refused with QUOTE_ORDER_MISMATCH on `quoteId`) with exactly one of `destinationAmount` and `sourceAmount`. The order is created at exactly the quoted amounts — the provider is not quoted again — and the response's `sourceAmount` is the crypto amount to send. `countryCode` may be omitted: the order takes the quote's (sent, it must match). Without a quoteId, `countryCode` is required (TRANSACTION_REQUEST_VALIDATION_ERROR). A quote creates one order, within 10 minutes of being issued. Checked before any provider call; a rejected order is not created:

| Code | HTTP | When |
|---|---|---|
| `QUOTE_EXPIRED` | 400 | The quoteId is unknown or another account's, was issued more than 10 minutes ago, or the provider's own quote behind it has expired. Request a new quote. |
| `QUOTE_ORDER_MISMATCH` | 400 | The quote has no quote from `serviceProvider`, or `sourceCurrencyCode`, `destinationCurrencyCode`, `countryCode`, `fiatPayoutMethod.type`, `destinationAmount` or `sourceAmount` differs from it (`errors` names the field), or the quote was already used (`errors`: `quoteId`), or it is not a partner quote (`errors`: `quoteId`). |

Name the bank with `details.bankIdentifier`, using a bank from `GET /network-partner/banks`: type `BANK_DIRECTORY_CODE` with its Meld `code` (`BANCOLOMBIA`), `NATIONAL_BANK_CODE` with its `nationalCode` (Colombia ACH `007`; leading zeros ignored), or `SWIFT_BIC` with its `swiftBic` (8 or 11 characters, for the order's country). Never send `bankCode`: it is the provider's code, which Meld fills from the identifier, and sending it, alone or with `bankIdentifier`, is `400 BENEFICIARY_DETAILS_INVALID`. An unknown type, a blank value, an identifier that names no bank the provider maps (a bank with no national code or BIC on file cannot be named by one), or a provider with no bank list for the country is `400 BANK_NOT_RESOLVED`. A payment method that needs a bank and has no identifier is `400 BANK_NOT_RESOLVED`. In each case no order is created. Invalid or missing payout details return `400 BENEFICIARY_DETAILS_INVALID`.

A rejected order does not use the quote up — rejected by Meld before reaching the provider (e.g. SOURCE_WALLET_INVALID) or refused by the provider (4xx): a corrected order on the same quoteId can follow. If the provider call fails (5xx) or times out, Meld asks the provider whether it created the payout: if so the order is created (201); if not, the quote stays used (the payout may still be in progress): request a new quote. Retrying with the same X-Idempotency-Key returns the first order.

Populated for NATIVE_TOKEN (Mercuryo) and VENDOR_SDK (Banxa), where the Meld SDK needs it to configure the sheet; null for PROVIDER_HOSTED (Coinbase). The VENDOR_SDK identifier is provider-scoped and NOT interchangeable with the NATIVE_TOKEN one: an Apple merchant id is bound to a single payment processing certificate, so crossing them yields tokens the processor cannot decrypt.

sdkSessionToken.description: The provider SDK's own session material, handed to the Meld SDK to present the sheet with — for Banxa, a Primer client token. Deliberately NOT sessionToken: that field authenticates Meld's paymentActions and /crypto/session/* endpoints, which this cannot do and must never be attempted with. Populated for VENDOR_SDK; null otherwise.

presentation.description: How this order's wallet surface is presented. The client dispatches on this and never on the service provider, so routing a new provider onto an existing shape needs no client change. Treat an unrecognised value as an unsupported order — the shapes are not interchangeable.

WalletOrder.description: Wallet response — the SESSION shape of a wallet method (APPLE_PAY, GOOGLE_PAY). THREE shapes. Dispatch on paymentMethodType plus the envelope's headlessPresentation (surface, protocol, version); `presentation` says which fields are populated. Never dispatch on the service provider, so a provider routed onto an existing shape needs no client change. The populated fields are disjoint per shape. NATIVE_TOKEN populates sessionToken + merchantTransactionId + merchantIdentifier: the caller renders the wallet sheet on its own surface, then continues through the order's paymentActions — POST to paymentActions.endpoint with the bearer that paymentActions.bearerTokenPointer names, using SUBMIT_WALLET_PAYMENT for the encrypted token, READ_SUBMISSION for the outcome, and VALIDATE_MERCHANT first when the descriptor lists it. The legacy /crypto/session/* Apple Pay endpoints remain for existing integrations. PROVIDER_HOSTED populates paymentLinkUrl — a provider-hosted URL that opens the wallet sheet directly when launched, with no intermediate screen. VENDOR_SDK populates sdkSessionToken + merchantIdentifier — the sheet belongs to the provider's own processor and is presented by the Meld SDK from that token; sessionToken is null and must not be substituted, since sdkSessionToken cannot authenticate paymentActions or the session endpoints.

Accepted spellings: UTC (2026-07-28T12:00:00Z), extended offset (2026-07-28T12:00:00+00:00) and basic offset (2026-07-28T12:00:00+0000), each with optional fractional seconds and with seconds themselves optional (2026-07-28T12:00Z). details.description: Payout fields. There is no predefined shape. Call `GET /supported/payment-methods/requirements` without a serviceProvider to get requirements for every provider. Optionally filter by serviceProvider. Send each published `key` that is not `derived`; Meld fills the derived ones. Name the bank with `bankIdentifier`, using a value from `GET /banks`: `{"type":"BANK_DIRECTORY_CODE","value":"BANCOLOMBIA"}` (the Meld `code`), `{"type":"NATIONAL_BANK_CODE","value":"007"}` (the `nationalCode`, such as Colombia's ACH code; leading zeros ignored) or `{"type":"SWIFT_BIC","value":"COLOCOBM"}` (the `swiftBic`, 8 or 11 characters). Never send `bankCode`: it is the provider's code, which Meld fills from the identifier, and sending it returns `BENEFICIARY_DETAILS_INVALID`. An identifier that names no bank the provider maps returns `BANK_NOT_RESOLVED`. Nested fields are nested objects (Network Partner `parentKey`), not dotted keys. Required keys are validated before any provider call.
